## SYSCALL INTERCEPTION
The Krynox eBPF-LSM module intercepted a `security_file_open` syscall on the primary Solana secret keypair. The process was attempting a raw read bypass.

## ATTACK VECTOR
Detected a **MITRE T1552** (Unsecured Credentials) pattern. The offending script utilized a symlink obfuscation technique, which was resolved in kernel-space via VFS dentry resolution.

## MITIGATION
Immediate SIGKILL issued. Zero-byte exfiltration confirmed. Hardware-level integrity maintained.

## SYSCALL INTERCEPTION
Intercepted at `vfs_open` layer. A malicious Python subprocess attempted to access the keypair through a nested symlink directory structure.

## ATTACK VECTOR
Corresponds to **T1036** (Masquerading). The attacker attempted to hide the target file path by using temporary directory redirects.

## MITIGATION
The Krynox eBPF module resolved the absolute inode target before the syscall was allowed to proceed. Process was terminated instantly.

## SYSCALL INTERCEPTION
Intercepted unauthorized access from a compromised npm dependency attempting to exfiltrate BIP39 seed phrases during a CI/CD build process.

## ATTACK VECTOR
Supply-chain injection. The process attempted to read the developer's default keypair and send it to a remote C2 server.

## MITIGATION
Kernel-level blocking prevented any network outbound traffic by terminating the parent process before the file read completion.

## SYSCALL INTERCEPTION
An unauthorized binary (`curl`) attempted to open the sensitive `id.json` file. This is a clear violation of Zero-Trust access policies.

## ATTACK VECTOR
Credential Theft attempt. Standard system utilities were being leveraged to exfiltrate private keys via a simple HTTP POST.

## MITIGATION
Krynox eBPF-LSM detected the process mismatch (Curl is not in the developer whitelist) and issued a kernel-level kill signal.
